# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

**Top pick: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900.** It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W output, a 10 ms UPS switchover and a 5-year warranty. Unlike the Bluetti Elite 200 V2, it can add a battery pack later to reach 4 kWh. That's roughly 23 hours of fridge, CPAP and router, by Outage Authority's math. Its $0.44/Wh is among the best in its class. ([Outage Authority roundup](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup), [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/))

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best budget | [Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) | $499 ($474.05 with code AFF5OFF) | 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, LiFePO4, 5-year warranty. Weighs 35 lb and can't be expanded. |
| Lightest | Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | $489 at Outbound Power (Jackery's own store: $559) | 1,070 Wh in 23.8 lb. About 12 hours of fridge, CPAP and router. Solar input is limited to 400 W. ([review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)) |
| Best value per Wh | Anker SOLIX F1500 | $599.99 | 1,536 Wh with 600W solar input. It tops [Compare Power Stations' ranking](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/) and is flagged as an unusually low price. |
| Alternative 2 kWh | Bluetti Elite 200 V2 | $899 or less | 2,074 Wh, 2,600 W and a 6,000-cycle battery, but no expansion. |

## Caveats

- **Elite 200 V2 pricing is inconsistent.** Two sources list it at $899, while Outage Authority says Bluetti ended its promotion and it's back at $1,199 (Amazon was $798.99 on Oct 7). It's only worth it if you see it at about $900 or less. Check the price before buying.
- **Prices change often.** The Bluetti Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh, $499) is [out of stock at Home Depot](https://www.homedepot.com/p/337557774).
- **Specs are manufacturer figures.** These sites say they haven't lab-tested the units, and most earn affiliate commissions. The Bluetti link above is an affiliate link.
- **Runtimes are estimates.** They assume a light load of about 77 W. A window AC, space heater or well pump will drain these much faster.

For a whole-house setup with 240V, you'd need to go above $1,000, such as the EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 at about $2,799.

If you tell me what you need to power (fridge, CPAP, AC, medical gear) and for how long, I can narrow it to one pick.
